candidates.label: W8 worker copy count 8 (period -1)
candidates.change: A and B worker: mov cl,9 -> mov cl,8 (zero-byte; each later rebuild is 1 turn shorter, copies template t3..t18, still covering the worker through call far). This has the same timing as any worker that is one instruction shorter.

candidates.label: W10 worker copy count 10 (period +1, control)
candidates.change: A and B worker: mov cl,9 -> mov cl,10 (zero-byte; rebuild 1 turn longer, copies 2 more zero bytes from private memory past the template)

threatFindings.threat: Rebuild exposure: a shorter worker (fewer instructions or copied words) cuts rebuild-phase deaths enough to gain overall
threatFindings.evidence: bbhin (1 turn shorter) ALL -0.012, multi -0.039, lead_V6 -0.22; A004 ou61i (2 turns shorter) ALL -0.030, strong -0.16
threatFindings.impact: Any exposure gain is smaller than the cost of changing the generation period. Do not shorten the worker unless the period is kept at 275 turns.

threatFindings.threat: The generation period (275 turns) is a local optimum versus same-family and multi-copy opponents
threatFindings.evidence: Both +1 and -1 turn lose: bbhin ALL -0.012 / multi -0.039; ooe05 ALL -0.017 / multi -0.054; lead_V6 -0.22 and -0.17 in both directions. lead_V4/zrl03 gain in both (+0.11..+0.20), which looks like desynchronization from those teams
threatFindings.impact: Period changes trade V6/multi-copy cohorts for V4/zrl03 cohorts and lose overall. Keep mov cl,9.

threatFindings.threat: Template/copy-count inconsistency (the rebuild copying junk or missing worker bytes)
threatFindings.evidence: Static check: the worker is 17 bytes (t0..t16) and the template is 9 words (t0..t17, t17 = next code byte). The rebuild copies t0 (MOVSB), t1..t2 (MOVSW), then t3..t20 with CX=9 (B's first copy CX=8 gives t3..t18). The minimal count is 7. Bytes t17..t20 land after call far and are never executed; private offsets 18..20 are zero and far from the pointer cells 2C0h/280h.
threatFindings.impact: Consistent, with no hidden bug. The extra copied words only add timing, which the period tests show is load-bearing.

threatFindings.threat: Instruction-level shortening (LES DI,[BX], dropping XOR SI / MOV CL / DEC DI) can remove a turn without side effects
threatFindings.evidence: Static analysis, no job. les di,[bx] is the same length and turn count as mov di,[bx]. dec di is needed because anchor+1 holds the trail's IP high byte. Removing xor si,si or mov cl would need a self-consistent SI/CX recurrence (SI_end = 3+2*CX), which has no solution. Any 1-turn removal has the timing tested in bbhin.
threatFindings.impact: There is no free shortening; the worker is effectively minimal for this rebuild scheme.

recommendation: Do not promote. Neither candidate is promising (ALL -0.012 and -0.017, multi clearly negative in both). The rev0 rebuild length/period is a local optimum (A004 already covered -2 turns; this covers -1 and +1). Close the worker-shortening card; future roles should not spend jobs on rebuild copy count or period.
